title: A Machine Learning Approach for Predicting Non-Suicidal Self-Injury in Young Adults
summary: In a 15-day ecological momentary assessment of 64 young adults, classification trees identified self-harm thoughts, sadness and frustration as informative predictors of non-suicidal self-injury thoughts or behaviors. The per-person averaged model achieved 84.78% accuracy but 14.48% positive predictive value, limiting any clinical-use interpretation.
ai_technology: CART classification of repeated app-based self-report features
organization: University of Vic–Central University of Catalonia; beHIT; Hospital Universitari d’Igualada; Universitat Autònoma de Barcelona

evidence.tested: Leave-one-subject-out evaluation reported 84.78% accuracy, 64.84% sensitivity, 85.53% specificity, 14.48% positive predictive value and 98.47% negative predictive value.
evidence.unknown: Small retrospective EMA cohort and low positive predictive value; no deployment or clinical-benefit validation.
evidence.ai_role: CART models classified repeated self-report features to predict non-suicidal self-injury thoughts or behaviors.

source_review.scope: Primary full-text Methods, Results and Discussion; date and exact-result catalog comparison checked.
